data.title: Singapore beats China in 4 CEE markets in country reputation index
data.description:
It ranked ahead of China in Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, and Slovenia.

Trust in Singapore amongst Central and Eastern European (CEE) consumers rose by 0.66 points between 2021 and 2026, according to the Rothman Consumer Reputation Index.

Singapore recorded one of the largest reputation gains amongst Asian countries tracked by the index, which measures the influence of the country of origin on purchasing decisions, Rothman Global said.

The country performed particularly well in Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, and Slovenia, where its country-of-origin score exceeded 6 and ranked ahead of China.

Singapore is one of the top four most reputable Asian countries amongst CEE’s 110 million consumers, alongside China, Japan, and South Korea.

Collectively, the four countries increased their average reputation score by 0.61 points.

The index found that 59% of CEE consumers consider a product’s country of origin when making purchases, compared with 55% who consider online reviews and 50% who prioritise the brand. 

Price remained the leading factor, cited by 86% of respondents.

The index tracks consumer perceptions across 10 CEE markets: Austria, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia, Bulgaria, and Serbia, Rothman Global said.

data.title: NHG Health unveils cluster-wide cancer institute in Singapore
data.description:
The hospital also signed two additional agreements.

NHG Health has launched the NHG Cancer Institute (NHGCI), a cluster-wide network spanning hospitals, polyclinics, primary care providers and community partners in Central and North Singapore.

NHGCI is anchored by Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Khoo Teck Puat Hospital and Woodlands Hospital, and covers care from screening through to survivorship and palliative care.

Planned expansions include radiotherapy at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, more chemotherapy services in the North and PET-CT diagnostics.  

Additionally, the hospital has signed a partnership with the Singapore Cancer Society (SCS) and Singtel Singapore, and will open its Centre for Precision and Genomic Medicine (CPGM).

Under its memorandum of understanding with SCS, NHG Health will expand screening and vaccination outreach to under-screened and higher-risk groups.

The two will also work on community-based rehabilitation, survivorship programmes, caregiver education and research.

Moreover, the CPGM will oversee NHG Health’s recruitment of 150,000 participants for Phase III of the National Precision Medicine Programme, which runs to 2031.

Further, the Singtel Singapore agreement, anchored by the Centre for Healthcare Innovation, will cover digitally enabled hospitals, virtual health and artificial intelligence.

data.title: Banks face earnings pressure amidst margin and wealth income concerns
data.description:
Higher bond yields could also weigh on REIT financing costs.

Singapore banks face pressure on earnings as concerns grow over lending margins and whether strong wealth-management income can be sustained.

“Higher global bond yields do not automatically translate into better bank profitability,” said Charu Chanana, Chief Investment Strategist at Saxo.

She said deposit costs, loan pricing, and Singapore-dollar interest rates will be key factors affecting banks' lending margins.

Concerns over bank earnings have contributed to the recent decline in the Straits Times Index, with banks leading the sell-off.

Chanana noted strong trading and wealth-related revenue have supported bank earnings, but these income streams can fluctuate with market conditions, potentially weighing on future earnings growth.

She added that the upcoming earnings season would be important in assessing whether banks can sustain their profitability.

Beyond banking, higher bond yields are also drawing attention to financing conditions in the REIT sector.

According to Saxo, debt costs, refinancing requirements and distribution sustainability remain key factors to watch for REITs.

“Higher yields also make fixed-income investments more competitive against dividend-paying stocks, an important consideration for Singapore's income-oriented market,” Chanana said.

The group identified investment in power infrastructure, data centres, advanced manufacturing, and semiconductor-related activities as areas creating opportunities beyond the traditional banking and property sectors.

data.title: SLNG starts construction of third LNG bunkering jetty
data.description:
Facility will support two MTPA of LNG bunker reload demand when completed in H2 2028.

Singapore LNG Corporation (SLNG) has begun construction of its third jetty at its terminal on Jurong Island, Singapore, to support growing demand for liquefied natural gas (LNG) bunkering.

SLNG broke ground on 9 October attended by SLNG Chairman Gan Seow Kee, CEO Leong Wei Hung, and Rotary Engineering Chairman Roger Chia.

The jetty, scheduled for completion in the second half of 2028, will support approximately 2 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of LNG bunker reload demand and accommodate break-bulk and other small-scale LNG operations.

It will handle LNG carriers ranging from 5,800 cubic metres to 80,000 cubic metres, making it SLNG’s first jetty dedicated to small- and mid-scale vessels.

With the new jetty and its existing infrastructure, SLNG could potentially support up to three MTPA of LNG bunker reloads, depending on market demand.

Separately, the SLNG Terminal has received International Sustainability and Carbon Certification EU (ISCC EU) certification for Bio-LNG handling.

The certification covers storage, regasification and send-out, bunkering and trucking services. It verifies that Bio-LNG handled through these services can be traced and accounted for under the ISCC EU framework.

SLNG is also working with partners to implement best practices in Bio-LNG certification and accounting across the upstream-to-terminal value chain to strengthen end-user confidence and support market adoption.

“As demand for LNG bunkering continues to grow, Jetty 3 will strengthen Singapore’s ability to support the next phase of growth and reinforce its position as a leading global bunkering and LNG trading hub,” Leong said.

He said the jetty would also expand the terminal’s capacity and operational flexibility to meet the maritime sector’s evolving energy needs.

data.title: OUE REIT confirms exclusive talks over One Raffles Place sale
data.description:
No binding agreement has been signed as negotiations remain ongoing.

OUE REIT has confirmed that it is in exclusive talks with entities linked to IOI Properties Group and CapitaLand Investment over the potential sale of One Raffles Place.

In a bourse filing on 8 October, the REIT’s manager clarified that negotiations and due diligence by the prospective buyers are ongoing, with no binding sale agreement signed.

The announcement follows a news report that IOI Properties and CapitaLand Investment were conducting exclusive due diligence for the acquisition of One Raffles Place.

OUE REIT's indirect subsidiary, OUB Centre Limited, holds an 81.54% interest in the property, whilst United Overseas Bank (UOB) owns the remaining 18.46%.

In February, the REIT announced that OUB Centre Limited and UOB were jointly conducting an exercise to determine market interest in the property.

The manager said it would make further announcements if there were any material developments, in accordance with Singapore Exchange listing requirements.

data.title: LTA proposes COE categories A and B merger under value-based system
data.description:
It is also seeking views on how Category E should be adjusted if the merger proceeds.

The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has proposed merging Certificate of Entitlement (COE) Categories A and B into one passenger car category, with a value-based fee-and-rebate system.

The authority is also seeking views on how Category E should be adjusted if the proposed merger proceeds.

The proposal aims to distinguish between mass-market and higher-value cars whilst allowing COE prices to continue to be determined by market forces.

LTA said that the review comes as advances in vehicle technology, particularly electric vehicles, have made engine capacity and power less effective in distinguishing between the two car segments.

It further noted that manufacturers are increasingly able to adjust vehicle specifications to meet existing Category A thresholds, resulting in more buyers competing for Category A COEs.

“Between February 2026 and June 2026, Category A COE prices have exceeded Category B prices on three occasions,” LTA added.

Engine capacity and power have been used to distinguish between mass-market and higher-value cars since 2014.

The proposal follows consultations with more than 200 members of the public, academics and automotive industry representatives, including focus group discussions held in April and May.

Other suggestions received include creating a separate COE category for private hire cars, introducing surcharges on multiple-car ownership, and allowing individuals to bid directly for certificates.

The public consultation runs from 8 October to 2 November.

LTA expects to complete its review by the end of the year and release its findings and recommendations in the first half of 2027.

data.title: British AI firm PhysicsX opens Singapore base, targets 100 staff
data.description:
It also signed a five-year, $40m AI development partnership with A*STAR.

British artificial intelligence (AI) firm PhysicsX has launched its Asia-Pacific hub in Singapore, targeting a team of over 100 simulation engineers and physics AI researchers.

The company said it plans to grow its local team beyond its current 20 employees over the next three years as it scales its presence across the region.

PhysicsX is collaborating with local public and private sector entities, including Seatrium
and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR).

Under a five-year, $40m partnership with A*STAR, the company will develop AI-powered engineering simulation capabilities to improve complex design and manufacturing processes across industries.

The launch was supported by Temasek and the Singapore Economic Development Board, PhysicsX said.

data.title: StarHub to acquire MyRepublic's Singapore mobile business
data.description:
Existing customers are being progressively migrated into the telco’s network.

StarHub will acquire MyRepublic's mobile business in Singapore, building on its investment in MyRepublic Broadband in 2021.

The move will bring MyRepublic's broadband and mobile businesses under the telco’s ownership, whilst retaining the mobile brand and its existing customer offerings.

Existing mobile customers will remain on their current plans and services without disruption as they are progressively migrated onto StarHub’s network.

The acquisition remains subject to both parties meeting the required conditions before completion.

StarHub CEO Nikhil Eapen said the consolidation would provide greater scale to invest more effectively in networks, resilience, and innovation.

Meanwhile, MyRepublic Group CEO Vaughan Baker said continuity and service quality remained the company's main priorities.

data.title: Fixed broadband revenue to rise 3% annually until 2030, GlobalData says
data.description:
Residential lines are forecast to expand faster at 3.6% over the same period.

Singapore’s fixed broadband revenue is forecast to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 3.1% from 2025 to 2031, driven by rising subscriptions and demand for multi-gigabit fiber plans, according to GlobalData.

Residential fixed broadband lines are forecast to grow at a 3.6% CAGR over the forecast period due to rising household demand for remote working, home entertainment, and smart-home connectivity.

Business fixed broadband revenue is forecast to grow at a 3% CAGR over the same period, GlobalData added.

This growth will be driven by enterprises adopting higher-capacity fiber plans to support cloud services, video collaboration, and data-intensive applications.

Fiber will account for 99.7% of fixed broadband lines in 2025 and maintain its near-total share through 2031, said Sarwat Zeeshan, an analyst at GlobalData.

Government-led network upgrades are accelerating the shift to multi-gigabit connectivity, including plans to deliver symmetrical 10Gbps speeds nationwide by 2026, she added.

“The government has committed up to $100m. By 2028, more than half a million households across the country are expected to benefit from the enhanced broadband infrastructure,” Zeeshan said.

Operators are expected to expand 10Gbps and Wi-Fi 7 bundles, fixed-mobile convergence offers, and security add-ons, she added.
